It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}) {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|ja|論社|qid=Q135022904}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine rank}} it was designated as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}. {{nihongo|'''Taka Shrine'''|多珂神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. It is located in {{ill|Mutsu Province|ca|Província de Mutsu|cs|Provincie Mucu|de|Provinz Mutsu|es|Provincia de Mutsu|fa|ولایت موتسو|fi|Mutsun provinssi|fr|Province de Mutsu|gl|Provincia de Mutsu|id|Provinsi Mutsu|it|Mutsu (provincia)|ja|陸奥国|ko|무쓰국|lt|Mucu žemė|nl|Mutsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Mutsu|ru|Муцу (провинция)|simple|Mutsu Province|sk|Mucu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Муцу|tr|Mutsu (vilayet)|uk|Муцу (провінція)|zh|陸奧國|zh_classical|陸奧國|zh_min_nan|Mutu-kok|zh_yue|陸奧國|qid=Q907389|lt=Mutsu Province}}.

== Enshrined Deity ==
* '''{{ill|Izanagi|abstract|Q813858|ar|إزاناغي|az|İzanaqi|bcl|Izanagi|bn|ইজানাগি|bs|Izanagi|ca|Izanagi|cs|Izanagi a Izanami|da|Izanagi|el|Ιζανάγκι|eo|Izanagi|es|Izanagi|fa|ایزاناگی|fi|Izanaki|fr|Izanagi|he|איזאנגי|hr|Izanagi|hu|Izanagi|id|Izanagi|it|Izanagi|ja|イザナギ|ka|იძანაგი|ko|이자나기|lt|Idzanagis|mk|Изанаги|mni|ꯏꯓꯥꯅꯥꯒꯤ|no|Izanagi|or|ଇଜାନାଗି|pt|Izanagi|ro|Izanagi|rsk|Изанаґи|ru|Идзанаги|simple|Izanagi|sk|Izanagi|sl|Izanagi|sr|Изанаки|sv|Izanagi|ta|இசநாகி|th|อิซานางิ|tl|Izanagi|tr|İzanagi|uk|Ідзанаґі|vi|Izanagi|zh|伊邪那岐|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}'''
*: According to *Ōsōshi*, a local historical record of the Sōma Domain, the shrine enshrines “Taka Ara-Mitama-no-Mikoto,” the {{ill|Mitama|de|Mitama|fa|میتاما|fr|Mitama|it|Mitama|ja|荒魂・和魂|ko|황혼과 화혼|pt|Mitama|ru|Митама|sr|Митама|th|มิตามะ|zh|荒魂與和魂|qid=Q495568|lt=Ara-mitama}} (rough spirit) of Izanagi-no-Mikoto.

The shintai (sacred object) has been prohibited from being viewed since ancient times and is therefore unknown. There is a theory that it may be a “hawk statue,” but this hawk statue is said to be the result of a mistaken transmission identifying the “White-Token Hawk” mentioned in shrine tradition as the shintai.

== History ==
== Overview ==
Taka Shrine is the foremost of the eight {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Engishiki-listed shrines}} in {{ill|Namekata district|ja|行方郡 (福島県)|qid=Q11626139}}, {{ill|Mutsu Province|ca|Província de Mutsu|cs|Provincie Mucu|de|Provinz Mutsu|es|Provincia de Mutsu|fa|ولایت موتسو|fi|Mutsun provinssi|fr|Province de Mutsu|gl|Provincia de Mutsu|id|Provinsi Mutsu|it|Mutsu (provincia)|ja|陸奥国|ko|무쓰국|lt|Mucu žemė|nl|Mutsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Mutsu|ru|Муцу (провинция)|simple|Mutsu Province|sk|Mucu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Муцу|tr|Mutsu (vilayet)|uk|Муцу (провінція)|zh|陸奧國|zh_classical|陸奧國|zh_min_nan|Mutu-kok|zh_yue|陸奧國|qid=Q907389}} (Taka Shrine, {{ill|Kashima Miko Shrine|ja|鹿島御子神社|qid=Q11677124}}, {{ill|Mito Shrine|ja|御刀神社|qid=Q11488802}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Masutamine Shrine}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Himatsuri Shrine}}, {{ill|Takakura Shrine|ja|高座神社|qid=Q11669904}}, {{ill|Sakamine Shrine|ja|冠嶺神社|qid=Q11395049}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Oshio Shrine}}). Among shrines bearing the name “Taga Shrine,” it is the only one nationwide to have been granted the rank of {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}, and it is said that Taga Shrines throughout the Tōhoku region originate from this shrine.

Although its exact origins are unknown, tradition holds that the shrine was founded in the 40th year of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|ar|الإمبراطور كيكو|arz|الامبراطور كيكو|azb|کیکو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Keikō|cs|Keikó|de|Keikō|es|Keikō Tennō|fa|امپراتور کیکو|fr|Keikō (empereur)|hr|Keikō|hu|Keikó japán császár|id|Kaisar Keikō|it|Keikō|ja|景行天皇|ka|კეიკო|ko|게이코 천황|nds|Keikō|nl|Keiko (keizer)|no|Keiko (keiser)|pl|Keikō|pt|Imperador Keikō|ru|Император Кэйко|sh|Car Keikō|simple|Emperor Keikō|sl|Cesar Kejko|sv|Keiko (kejsare)|th|จักรพรรดิเคโก|tl|Emperador Keikō|tr|Keikō (imparator)|uk|Імператор Кейко|uz|Imperator Keikō|vi|Thiên hoàng Keikō|yo|Emperor Keikō|zh|景行天皇|zh_min_nan|Keikô Thian-hông|zh_yue|景行天皇|qid=Q329723}} by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|arz|ياماتو تاكيرو|be|Ямата Такэру|de|Yamatotakeru|es|Yamato Takeru|fa|یاماتو تاکه‌رو|fr|Yamato Takeru|hu|Jamatotakeru|id|Yamato Takeru|it|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|ko|야마토타케루|pt|Yamato Takeru|ru|Ямато Такэру|sh|Yamato Takeru|simple|Yamato Takeru|sq|Jamato Takeru|sr|Јамато Такеру|sv|Yamato Takeru|tr|Yamato Takeru|uk|Ямато Такеру|ur|یاماتو تاکیرو|vi|Yamato Takeru|zh|日本武尊|zh_min_nan|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}}, who visited this area during his eastern campaign and enshrined the deity to pray for victory in battle. To the northwest of the current location lies the Furuuchi area, through which the Ōta River flows, and there is said to be a place called “Daimyōjin Kawara.” The ancient shrine site is said to have been on the southern hills of Daimyōjin Kawara. In the 7th year, 2nd month of {{ill|Emperor Chūai|ar|الإمبراطور تشواي|arz|الامبراطور تشواى|azb|چوای (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Chūai|cs|Čúai|de|Chūai|es|Chūai Tennō|fa|امپراتور چوآی|fr|Chūai|hr|Chūai|hu|Csúai japán császár|id|Kaisar Chūai|it|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇|ka|ტიუაი|ko|주아이 천황|nl|Chuai|pl|Chūai|pt|Chuai|ru|Император Тюай|sh|Car Chūai|simple|Emperor Chūai|sl|Cesar Čuaj|sv|Chuai|th|จักรพรรดิชูไอ|tl|Emperador Chūai|tr|Chūai (imparator)|uk|Імператор Тюай|uz|Imperator Chūai|vi|Thiên hoàng Chūai|zh|仲哀天皇|zh_min_nan|Tyûai Thian-hông|zh_yue|仲哀天皇|qid=Q179971}}, a violent storm washed away and severely damaged the shrine buildings, which drifted to the banks of the nearby Ōta River. In the 9th month of the same year, the shrine was relocated to Ashinodaira (present-day Jō-no-uchi, the current site).

In Kōryaku 2 ({{ill|1380|ab|1380|af|1380|als|1380|am|1380 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1380|ar|1380|ary|1380|arz|1380|ast|1380|avk|1380|az|1380|azb|۱۳۸۰ (میلادی)|ban|1380|be|1380|be_x_old|1380|bg|1380|bn|১৩৮০|bpy|মারি ১৩৮০|br|1380|bs|1380.|ca|1380|cdo|1380 nièng|ceb|1380|ckb|١٣٨٠|crh|1380|cs|1380|cv|1380|cy|1380|da|1380|de|1380|diq|1380|el|1380|eml|1380|eo|1380|es|1380|et|1380|eu|1380|fa|۱۳۸۰ (میلادی)|fi|1380|fo|1380|fr|1380|frr|1380|fy|1380|ga|1380|gan|1380年|gcr|1380|gd|1380|gl|1380|gv|1380|he|1380|hi|१३८०|hr|1380.|hsb|1380|ht|1380 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1380|hy|1380|id|1380|ilo|1380|io|1380|is|1380|it|1380|ja|1380年|jv|1380|ka|1380|kaa|1380|kk|1380 жыл|ko|1380년|la|1380|lb|1380|lij|1380|lmo|1380|lt|1380 m.|lv|1380. gads|mai|१३८०|map_bms|1380|mdf|1380|mg|1380|mhr|1380|mi|1380|min|1380|mk|1380|mr|इ.स. १३८०|mrj|1380 и|ms|1380|my|၁၃၈၀|mzn|۱۳۸۰|nap|1380|nds|1380|nds_nl|1380|new|सन् १३८०|nl|1380|nn|1380|no|1380|nrm|1380|nso|1380|oc|1380|or|୧୩୮୦|os|1380-æм аз|pl|1380|pnb|1380|pt|1380|qu|1380|ro|1380|ru|1380 год|rue|1380|sa|१३८०|sah|1380|scn|1380|sd|1380ع|se|1380|sh|1380.|shn|1380|simple|1380|sk|1380|sl|1380|smn|1380|sq|1380|sr|1380|su|1380|sv|1380|sw|1380|tg|Соли 1380|th|พ.ศ. 1923|tk|1380|tl|1380|tly|1380|tr|1380|tt|1380 ел|uk|1380|ur|1380ء|uz|1380|vec|1380|vi|1380|war|1380|wuu|1380年|xmf|1380|zh|1380年|zh_classical|一三八〇年|zh_min_nan|1380 nî|zh_yue|1380年|qid=Q6327}}), there existed a bronze bell (waniguchi) bearing an inscription of donation by Fujiwara Yoshimori, which is said to hang in the inner sanctuary of the main hall. From April of Jōō 4, Kinoe-mi year ({{ill|1655|ab|1655|af|1655|als|1655|am|1655 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1655|ar|1655|ary|1655|arz|1655|ast|1655|avk|1655|az|1655|azb|۱۶۵۵ (میلادی)|ban|1655|bcl|1655|be|1655|be_x_old|1655|bg|1655|bn|১৬৫৫|bpy|মারি ১৬৫৫|br|1655|bs|1655.|ca|1655|cdo|1655 nièng|ceb|1655|ckb|١٦٥٥|co|1655|crh|1655|cs|1655|cv|1655|cy|1655|da|1655|de|1655|diq|1655|el|1655|eml|1655|eo|1655|es|1655|et|1655|eu|1655|fa|۱۶۵۵ (میلادی)|fi|1655|fo|1655|fr|1655|frp|1655|frr|1655|fur|1655|fy|1655|ga|1655|gan|1655年|gcr|1655|gd|1655|gl|1655|gv|1655|he|1655|hi|१६५५|hr|1655.|hsb|1655|ht|1655 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1655|hy|1655|hyw|1655 թուական|ia|1655|id|1655|ilo|1655|io|1655|is|1655|it|1655|ja|1655年|jv|1655|ka|1655|kaa|1655|kk|1655 жыл|kn|೧೬೫೫|ko|1655년|krc|1655 джыл|la|1655|lb|1655|li|1655|lij|1655|lmo|1655|lt|1655 m.|lv|1655. gads|mai|१६५५|map_bms|1655|mdf|1655|mg|1655|mhr|1655|mi|1655|mk|1655|ml|1655|mr|इ.स. १६५५|mrj|1655 и|ms|1655|my|၁၆၅၅|mzn|۱۶۵۵|nap|1655|nds|1655|new|सन् १६५५|nl|1655|nn|1655|no|1655|nrm|1655|nso|1655|oc|1655|olo|1655|or|୧୬୫୫|os|1655-æм аз|pl|1655|pnb|1655|pt|1655|qu|1655|ro|1655|ru|1655 год|rue|1655|sa|१६५५|sah|1655|scn|1655|sd|1655ع|se|1655|sh|1655.|shn|1655|si|1655|simple|1655|sk|1655|sl|1655|smn|1655|sq|1655|sr|1655|su|1655|sv|1655|sw|1655|szl|1655|ta|1655|te|1655|tg|Соли 1655|th|พ.ศ. 2198|tk|1655|tl|1655|tly|1655|tr|1655|tt|1655 ел|uk|1655|ur|1655ء|uz|1655|vec|1655|vi|1655|vls|1655|wa|1655|war|1655|wuu|1655年|xmf|1655|yi|1655|zh|1655年|zh_min_nan|1655 nî|zh_yue|1655年|qid=Q6975}}) to Meireki 1 (the same year), the shrine sanctuary was repaired, with timber donated by {{ill|Sōma Tadatane|ja|相馬忠胤|ko|소마 다다타네|qid=Q8514579}}. During the {{ill|Genroku|ar|فترة غنروكو|cs|Genroku|de|Genroku|es|Genroku|fa|گنروکو|fr|Ère Genroku|id|Genroku|it|Genroku|ja|元禄|ko|겐로쿠|pt|Genroku|ru|Гэнроку|simple|Genroku|sk|Genroku|sr|Генроку|sv|Genroku|tr|Genroku|zh|元祿|qid=Q1325001}} era, {{ill|Sōma Masatane|ja|相馬昌胤|ko|소마 마사타네 (1661년)|qid=Q8514599}} built a sanctuary called “Yōshinden,” associated with {{ill|Yoshida Shintō|de|Yoshida-Shintō|fa|یوشیدا شینتو|fr|Shinto Yoshida|ja|吉田神道|ru|Ёсида синто|qid=Q1760351}}, within the castle grounds, and at that time, for certain reasons, had a statue of the “White-Token Hawk” carved and dedicated to Taka Shrine. This wooden statue of the “White-Token Hawk” is said to have been stored in a miniature shrine. Even today, the “White-Token Hawk Statue” is enshrined in the main hall as a sacred treasure. According to shrine tradition, although it appears to be an ordinary wooden statue, it was named “White-Token Hawk” because the feathers appear white depending on how the light strikes them.

In Kyōhō 9 ({{ill|1724|ab|1724|af|1724|als|1724|am|1724 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1724|ar|1724|ary|1724|arz|1724|ast|1724|avk|1724|az|1724|azb|۱۷۲۴ (میلادی)|ba|1724 йыл|ban|1724|bar|1724|bcl|1724|be|1724|be_x_old|1724|bg|1724|bn|১৭২৪|bo|༡༧༢༤ལོ།|bpy|মারি ১৭২৪|br|1724|bs|1724.|ca|1724|cdo|1724 nièng|ce|1724 шо|ceb|1724|ckb|١٧٢٤|co|1724|crh|1724|cs|1724|csb|1724|cv|1724|cy|1724|da|1724|de|1724|diq|1724|el|1724|eml|1724|eo|1724|es|1724|et|1724|eu|1724|fa|۱۷۲۴ (میلادی)|fi|1724|fo|1724|fr|1724|frp|1724|frr|1724|fur|1724|fy|1724|ga|1724|gan|1724年|gcr|1724|gd|1724|gl|1724|gv|1724|he|1724|hi|१७२४|hr|1724.|hsb|1724|ht|1724 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1724|hy|1724|hyw|1724 թուական|ia|1724|id|1724|ilo|1724|io|1724|is|1724|it|1724|ja|1724年|jv|1724|ka|1724|kaa|1724|kk|1724 жыл|kn|೧೭೨೪|ko|1724년|krc|1724 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1724|la|1724|lb|1724|lez|1724 йис|li|1724|lij|1724|lmo|1724|lt|1724 m.|lv|1724. gads|mai|१७२४|map_bms|1724|mdf|1724|mg|1724|mhr|1724|mi|1724|min|1724|mk|1724|mr|इ.स. १७२४|mrj|1724 и|ms|1724|my|၁၇၂၄|myv|1724 ие|mzn|۱۷۲۴|nah|1724|nap|1724|nds|1724|new|सन् १७२४|nl|1724|nn|1724|no|1724|nrm|1724|nso|1724|oc|1724|olo|1724|or|୧୭୨୪|os|1724-æм аз|pl|1724|pnb|1724|pt|1724|qu|1724|ro|1724|ru|1724 год|rue|1724|sa|१७२४|sah|1724 сыл|sc|1724|scn|1724|sd|1724ع|se|1724|sh|1724.|shn|1724|simple|1724|sk|1724|sl|1724|smn|1724|sq|1724|sr|1724|su|1724|sv|1724|sw|1724|szl|1724|ta|1724|te|1724|tg|Соли 1724|th|พ.ศ. 2267|tk|1724|tl|1724|tly|1724|tr|1724|tt|1724 ел|uk|1724|ur|1724ء|uz|1724|vec|1724|vi|1724|vls|1724|vo|1724|wa|1724|war|1724|wuu|1724年|xmf|1724|yi|1724|zea|1724|zh|1724年|zh_min_nan|1724 nî|zh_yue|1724年|qid=Q6926}}), Sōma Masatane donated shrine lands amounting to 1 koku and 9 to, among other offerings, and the shrine received deep reverence from successive lords of the Sōma Domain.

nî|zh_yue|1944年|qid=Q5268}}), it was elevated to a prefectural shrine.

Taka Shrine has long been believed to bestow divine benefits such as longevity, fulfillment of wishes, household safety, safe childbirth, maritime safety, and abundant catches. Because it was originally enshrined to pray for victory in battle, many worshippers in particular visit to pray for certain victory in elections.

== Shrine Buildings ==
* Main Hall – Built in one-bay nagare-zukuri style, with side screens and balustrades. Dragon carvings are applied to the side screens.

'''Interior of the Heiden'''

The coffered lattice ceiling of the heiden is decorated with polychrome paintings of animals, plants, and human figures. Only during the first three days of the New Year, a goma altar is set up in front of the main hall doors within the heiden, where goma fire rituals are performed. During these rituals, prayers are offered by holding amulets and votive items directly over the sacred flames.

File:Gomadan of Taka-jinja shrine.JPG|Goma altar at Taka Shrine<br/>Only during the New Year period, a tree called “Nodeppō” is used as goma sticks for the ritual.

'''Interior of the Worship Hall'''

Inside the worship hall are housed items such as an ema depicting “Izanagi-no-Mikoto and Izanami-no-Mikoto,” paintings of hawks, and a plaque reading “Protection of the State,” dedicated in Meiji 38 to commemorate the {{ill|Siege of Port Arthur|ar|حصار ميناء آرثر|azb|پورت آرتور موحاصیره‌سی|bg|Обсада на Порт Артур|cs|Obléhání Port Arturu|de|Belagerung von Port Arthur|es|Asedio de Port Arthur|fa|محاصره پورت آرتور|fi|Port Arthurin piiritys|fr|Siège de Port-Arthur|id|Pengepungan Port Arthur|it|Assedio di Port Arthur|ja|旅順攻囲戦|ko|여순항 포위전|nl|Beleg van Port Arthur|pl|Obrona Port Artur|pt|Cerco de Port Arthur|ro|Asediul de la Port Arthur|ru|Оборона Порт-Артура|sh|Opsada Port Artura|sk|Obliehanie prístavu Port Arthur|sr|Опсада Порт Артура|sv|Belägringen av Port Arthur|th|การปิดล้อมพอร์ตอาร์เธอร์|uk|Облога Порт-Артура|zh|旅順會戰|qid=Q210800|lt=Fall of Port Arthur}} during the Russo-Japanese War.

== Other Structures ==
* Stone statues of the Seven Lucky Gods
* Near the sacred tree behind the main hall, Buddhist statues from the era of syncretism between Shinto and Buddhism are placed.

== Approach ==
Along the approach is a sacred pond, and on the small central island stand a small shrine of Kogota Yamatsumi Shrine and a stone monument of Konpira Shrine. The first torii gate stands southeast of {{ill|Iwaki-Ōta Station|id|Stasiun Iwaki-Ōta|ja|磐城太田駅|ko|이와키오타역|my|အိဝခိ - အိုးတဘူတာ|ur|ایواکی-اوٹا اسٹیشن|zh|磐城太田車站|qid=Q6100384}}, along the tracks of the {{ill|Jōban Line|de|Jōban-Linie|es|Línea Jōban|fa|خط جوبان|fr|Ligne Jōban|it|Linea Jōban|ja|常磐線|ko|조반선|ru|Линия Дзёбан|th|สายโจบัง|tl|Linyang Jōban|zh|常磐線|qid=Q1369263}}.

== Subsidiary and Branch Shrines ==
* Yasaka-Inari Shrine
*: The shrine building reuses the former main hall of Taka Shrine, and within it are enshrined Yasaka Shrine and Inari Shrine. Yasaka Shrine was formerly called Gozu Tennō Shrine and had been located in the Jō-no-uchi area, the present location. According to *Ōsōshi*, the sacred object of Yasaka Shrine measures 7 sun in length. Inari Shrine was formerly located in the Oinari area southeast of the current site and was later enshrined together with Yasaka Shrine.
*: On the east side of the shrine building are a sacred cedar tree, Raijin Shrine, and a stone monument of Aomasa Daigongen (Aomasa Shrine).
* Raijin Shrine
*: The sacred object is recorded as measuring 7 sun in length.
* Aomasa Daigongen (Aomasa Shrine) Stone Monument
*: The enshrined deities are Amaterasu Ōmikami, Tsukuyomi-no-Kami, and Ame-no-Minakanushi-no-Kami. It was transferred from {{ill|Aoso Shrine|ja|青麻神社|qid=Q11662833}} in Iwakiri, Miyagino Ward, Sendai City, Miyagi Prefecture.

It is enshrined near Sōma Odaka Shrine in Odaka Ward, Minamisōma City. The enshrined deities are Takaokami-no-Kami and Yamiokami-no-Kami.

== History ==
The founding date of Kifune Shrine is unknown, but it is said to have been worshipped since before Genkō 3 (1323). According to *Ōsōshi*, there is a record stating that the box housing the sacred object bears an inscription indicating it was made in the 5th year of Hōen, kinoe-mi year, 8th month. The sacred object is said to be a statue “riding a dragon and wearing white robes.” In Bunji 5, when {{ill|Sōma Moritsune|ja|相馬師常|qid=Q11582495}} took control of Namekata District, he designated Kifune Shrine as the district’s chief shrine and deeply revered it, carrying out embellishments of the shrine buildings. Kifune Shrine was mainly worshipped as a deity of rainmaking and stopping rain, bountiful harvests, success and advancement in life, and martial arts.

According to *Ōsōshi*, Taka Shrine once existed within the precincts of Kibune (Kifune) Shrine in Minami-Odaka Village. It was a shrine building measuring 2 shaku 5 sun in depth. It was a shrine enshrined during the era of Emperor Keikō, with Izanagi-no-Mikoto and Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto as the two main deities, and Koyō Myōjin as an accompanying deity.

In Bunka 12 (1815), the lord of the Sōma Domain, {{ill|Sōma Masutane|ja|相馬益胤|ko|소마 마스타네|qid=Q8514605}}, ordered shrine priests and a man named Watanabe Yoshitsuna to investigate and identify the eight Shikinaisha in Namekata District. Watanabe Yoshitsuna reported that the Engishiki-listed Myōjin Taisha known as Taka Shrine was the Taka Daimyōjin enshrined within the grounds of Kōmyō-ji Temple in Taka Village. In response, Takadama Tanba, a shrine priest of the Kibune Shrine in Odaka Village, submitted a counter-report claiming that Taka Shrine was a small shrine enshrined in Odaka Village.

According to that report, Taka Shrine was a shrine where the Yasakani no Magatama, one of the Three Sacred Treasures, was enshrined as the local tutelary deity, and it had long been the guardian deity of Odaka Village. The ancestors of the shrine priest family originally bore the name “Takadama,” but out of deference to Taka Shrine they changed it to “Takadama.” The Taga faith’s head shrine, {{ill|Taga-taisha|el|Τάγκα-τάισα|fr|Taga-taisha|ja|多賀大社|tr|Taga-taisha|zh|多賀大社|qid=Q402091}} in Shiga Prefecture, is called “O-Taga-sama,” and the name Odaka is said to derive from calling the enshrined Taka Shrine “Mi-Taka.” The Takadama family administered the rites of both Kifune Shrine and Taka Shrine, which were enshrined near {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sōma Odaka Shrine}} in Odaka Ward. Taka Shrine was located at a place called Nihonmatsu in Odaka Village, about ten ken from Kifune Shrine. Later, Taka Shrine was washed away by a flood during the Genroku era, but a farmer recovered the small shrine from the water and it was enshrined together within the precincts of Kifune Shrine.

Takadama Tanba wrote down the above origins of Taka Shrine in Odaka Village and reported them to the domain. However, according to the compiler of *Ōsōshi*:
* In shrine identification surveys conducted before the domain’s Bunka 12 investigation, Taka Shrine of Odaka Village is not recorded.
* Records of the Shima family, shrine priests of Taka Shrine in Taka Village, appear in shrine priest registries from Genroku 15 and in temple and shrine surveys from the Shōtoku era, whereas records of the Takadama family only appear from Kanpō 1 onward.

For these reasons, the theory of Takadama Tanba is said to contain many doubtful points.

At present, the inscription on the stone monument describing the shrine’s origins at the entrance of Kifune Shrine’s approach states that the enshrined deities are Takaokami-no-Kami and Yamiokami-no-Kami, and that Taka Shrine is enshrined together in the same sanctuary.
